# ClayPT

> ClayPT (Clay Path Tracing) is a progressive, physically based path tracer for the browser. npm package `claypt`. WebGPU with a WebGL 2 fallback, OpenPBR 1.1 materials, TinyBVH (WebAssembly) acceleration, and Intel Open Image Denoise (OIDN) denoising. MIT licensed.

## Usage essentials

- Install: `npm install claypt` (+ `three` for the Three.js helpers). ESM with TypeScript declarations; every option has TSDoc with its default.
- A scene is a plain object `{ meshes: Mesh[], lights: SceneLight[], background? }`. A `Mesh(geometry, material)` is placed with `mesh.matrixWorld` (column-major mat4, gl-matrix compatible).
- `const renderer = new Renderer({ canvas }); renderer.setSize(w, h);` then call `renderer.render(scene, camera)` once per `requestAnimationFrame`. It accumulates samples up to `renderer.maxSamples` (default 2048) and returns a status.
- Statuses: PREPARING (6, device init / BVH build), COMPILING_SHADER (1), RENDERING (2), DENOISING (3), FINISHED (4), ERROR (5). Keep calling `render()` through PREPARING and COMPILING_SHADER.
- Scene membership, mesh matrix elements, geometry/material references, light parameters and background values are detected automatically on each render. After material parameter edits call `material.markUpdated()`; after geometry attribute edits call `geometry.markUpdated()`; after texture pixel or UV-array element edits call `texture.markUpdated()`. Camera and renderer options are checked every frame. WebGPU refits transform-only changes; WebGL rebuilds mesh data for transforms.
- Three.js: `const sync = new THREESceneSync(threeScene);` then `sync.update(); renderer.render(sync.scene, fromTHREECamera(threeCamera));` each frame. `sync.dispose()` releases conversion caches. `fromTHREEScene(threeScene)` is a one-shot conversion with fresh objects on every call. Three.js attribute/index edits require `needsUpdate = true`; texture pixel edits require `texture.needsUpdate = true`. Supports MeshStandardMaterial / MeshPhysicalMaterial / MeshBasicMaterial; directional, point, spot, rect-area and ambient lights; `scene.environment` as an equirectangular float DataTexture. Prefer Three.js GLTFLoader over the built-in `loadGLTF`.
- Materials: `OpenPBRMaterial` with OpenPBR names (`baseColor`, `baseMetalness`, `specularRoughness`, `specularIor`, `transmissionWeight`, `coatWeight`, `subsurfaceWeight`, `fuzzWeight`, `thinFilmWeight`, `emissionLuminance`, ...). Colors are linear RGB; 8-bit textures are sRGB.
- Lights: `RectLight(size, color, intensity)` emits along its local -Z; `SphereLight(position, color, intensity, radius)`; `SpotLight(position, direction, color, intensity, radius, innerDeg, outerDeg)`; `DirectionalLight(position, color, intensity)` shines from `position` toward the origin; `EnvironmentLight(texture)` for equirectangular HDR (`await loadRGBE(url)`).
- Backgrounds: omit to show the environment; `[r, g, b, a]` linear color (`[0,0,0,0]` = transparent canvas, pair with `material.shadowCatcher = true`); a `Texture`; or `{ type: 'GroundedSkybox', map, height, radius }`.
- Denoising (WebGPU only): `await renderer.setDenoiser({ model: 'standard' | 'small' | 'cleanAuxLarge', weightsBaseUrl?, realtime? })`. Weights default to jsDelivr for the installed version; self-host `node_modules/claypt/oidn/weights/` in production.
- Final stills: `await renderer.renderOfflineFrame(scene, camera, { samples })`, then `renderer.prepareForExport()` and `canvas.toBlob(...)`. Linear HDR pixels: `await renderer.getRawOutput()`.
- BVHs build automatically with TinyBVH before the first frame; `await renderer.prepareScene(scene)` builds up front.

## Common pitfalls

- Material parameter, geometry attribute or texture pixel edits require the edited object’s `markUpdated()`. Mesh transforms and scene membership changes need no extra call.
- `createPlaneGeometry()` is 2×2 in XZ; `createSphereGeometry()` and `createCubeGeometry()` span -1..1. Scale with `matrixWorld`.
- Rect lights are one-sided; rotate them to face the scene.
- OIDN, auto exposure, HDR output and the `neutral` tone mapper require WebGPU.
- Call `renderer.setSize` with drawing-buffer pixels and update `camera.aspect` on resize.
